newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes roll with June paper expiry, end lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes roll with June paper expiry, end lower.

text.p: Paper crude expiration pushed U.S. cash crude prices lower on Tuesday, but outright crude values rolled along a volatile course before trading settled.
Cash dealers said domestic grade markets featured talk of how much foreign crude would be delivered against the June NYMEX contract, a situation which will not clear until later this week.
June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing talked late around 40 cents weaker, at $21.15-25 a barrel. June contracts lost some ground to July, putting the June/July roll at -40 cents.
June Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) were pegged around a 15 cents premium in the afternoon, after climbing to a plateau of 25 cents on Monday.

EFPs are protection for refiners from getting stuck with uneconomical and possibly unusable foreign crude deliveries. EFPs, which allow a buyer or seller to exchange a futures position for physical positions, have gained as a result of the virtual escape from paper positions.
For grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James remained around a two cents discount to marker WTI, with Midland/WTI at last deals from 41-42 cents under June WTI/Cushing.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire sold at minus 55 and 60 cents to the benchmark.
West Texas Sour/Midland was relatively steady, selling at discounts between $1.42-1.50. Late talk weakened the market to a range from $1.54-45 under WTI.
Eugene Island sours sold between $1.35 and $1.45 under benchmark, and talked late at minus $1.60-1.40.
Some negative expectations for Tuesday's American Petroleum Institute (API) inventory report pushed outright prices lower, along with expiration-related technical selling, traders said.
